# ruststream-amqp

> `ruststream-amqp` is the AMQP 1.0 broker crate for RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them. AMQP 1.0 is an ISO standard, so one crate over the `fe2o3-amqp` client serves ActiveMQ Artemis and Classic, RabbitMQ 4.x, Azure Service Bus and Event Hubs, Amazon MQ, Solace, Apache Qpid and IBM MQ.

A subscription is the descriptor `AmqpAddress`: `AmqpAddress::queue` (anycast), `AmqpAddress::topic` (multicast) or `AmqpAddress::raw` (a verbatim address), with the settings of its link. A service file imports `ruststream_amqp::prelude::*`, which offers `AmqpPublish` as `Publish` along with the broker, its SASL profile and the capability traits `RequestReply` and, with the `transaction` feature, `TransactionalPublisher`.

This site holds the guides, one page per component and the architecture of the crate; the API reference is on docs.rs, and the framework itself is documented on the RustStream site.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-amqp/latest/): building an AMQP 1.0 service with the crate

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-amqp/latest/architecture/): how AMQP 1.0 works, where the crate sits between the broker and the RustStream runtime, and what that costs
- [Benchmarks](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-amqp/latest/architecture/benchmarks/): what this crate and the framework's runtime cost over the raw `fe2o3-amqp` client, and how to re-measure it with `just bench`
